To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the health of Swedish-speaking Finnish children is better than that among Finnish-speaking Finnish children.
the health of Swedish-speaking schoolchildren is better than that among Finnish-speaking schoolchildren.
the health of Finnish-speaking schoolchildren is better than that reported in earlier studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the health advantage of Swedish-speakers in Finland is a consequence of their social status, or whether it is a phenomenon that has its roots in the linguistic group itself.
the health advantage of Swedish-speakers and its possible determinants.
the health advantage of the Swedish-speaking population in Finland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Swedish-speaking children in Finland perceive their health as being better than that of children of the same age in the Finnish-speaking population.
the Swedish-speaking children are healthier than Finnish-speaking children, but the reason for the difference is unknown.
the health advantage of Swedish speakers is not explained by any of the known risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the health advantage of Swedish speaking children is not explained by the variables studied.
the health advantage of Swedish-speakers is not explained by differences in health behaviours, socioeconomic background or social relationships.
the health advantage of the Swedish-speaking population in Finland seems to be independent of known risk factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health advantage of Swedish speaking children in Finland cannot be attributed to socioeconomic status, social relationships or lifestyle factors.
the health advantage of Swedish-speakers cannot be attributed to socioeconomic factors, social relationships, or health behaviour.
differences in health between Finnish- and Swedish-speakers cannot be explained by socioeconomic background, social relations or health behaviour.
